metadata.title: Three Workflows, and What Separates Them
metadata.purpose: Show how the five packages combine into three end-to-end workflows, and spend the time on what distinguishes them rather than narrating every step. Explains a proposal; does not advocate for it.

beats.narration_text: Part one laid out five packages. This is how they combine — three end to end workflows. What matters is not the steps, but what separates them.
beats.new_visual_element: The ask — how do the five fit together

props.command: how do the five packages fit together?
props.segment: Three Workflows, and What Separates Them

beats.narration_text: Three workflows. A prevents. B describes. C organises what B described. They are not three versions of the same thing, and not a menu to pick one from.
beats.new_visual_element: The three named, with the verb each one owns

beats.narration_text: Workflow A. The fellow pastes the starter block, builds as normal, and renders. The toolkit checks the size it is about to write, and if it is not one of the two approved sizes it stops and says what is wrong. Nothing is saved. They fix it, re-render, run the self check, and upload.
beats.new_visual_element: Workflow A as a flow, with the refusal looping back

beats.narration_text: Workflow B runs on a schedule and touches nothing. It lists every file from the Drive's own record, so the whole folder is read in seconds without downloading anything. Fellow, format and resolution come from the filename. The fast checks run first, and anything failing there goes no further. Only what passes gets downloaded for the slower frame check.
beats.new_visual_element: Workflow B as a funnel — the cheap pass first, then the expensive one

beats.narration_text: Workflow C. Every step of B runs first, so the verdicts are settled before anything moves. Files go into two folders made by hand in advance. A note sits beside each failing file with the corrected value, the fellow is sent that same line, and every move is logged.
beats.new_visual_element: Workflow C — B's verdicts, then the routing, with the log underneath

beats.narration_text: What separates them. A never creates the wrong file, so nothing downstream sees it. B changes nothing and prevents nothing — it exists so that no one has to open a video to find out whether it is usable. C is the only one that writes, and it adds no information B did not already have.
beats.new_visual_element: One line each — what only this workflow does

beats.narration_text: So the order is the argument. A sits upstream of B. C only makes sense once B is trusted. Someone could run all three, or only B, or only A. What they should not do is treat them as three bids for the same job.
beats.new_visual_element: A upstream of B, C downstream of trust — not three parallel options

beats.narration_text: One thing to state plainly. Our own submission guidance says the definitive four K check happens on YouTube, after processing, because a local file cannot prove how YouTube will handle it. None of this removes that. What it removes is the upload cycles spent on videos that were never going to pass.
beats.new_visual_element: The check that stays, and the cycles that go

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you run this review, the question is which of the three you would trust first, and whether you would rather be told earlier, or told less often.
beats.new_visual_element: The handoff question, typed into the composer
